title: Arsenal's Long Wait: Can Mikel Arteta Finally Deliver the Premier League Title?
summary: Arsenal have come agonisingly close to the Premier League title in recent seasons, finishing second twice with record-breaking points tallies. As the 2026-27 season begins, the question is whether this is finally their year.
content:
There is a particular kind of hope that Arsenal fans have learned to carry — the hope that comes from being genuinely good, good enough to believe, good enough to dream, but not quite good enough to deliver at the final moment. It is not the hope of the perennial underdog. It is the hope of a team that knows it is close, that can see the prize clearly, and that keeps finding new ways to fall just short.

Mikel Arteta's Arsenal have been the Premier League's nearly team. Second in 2022-23 with 84 points. Second in 2023-24. The gap between Arsenal and the title has been measured not in quality but in moments — a dropped point here, an injury at the wrong time, a Manchester City performance that seemed to exceed the laws of football.

What Has Changed

The squad that Arteta has assembled at the Emirates is the strongest in a generation. Bukayo Saka — still only 24 — is one of the best wide players in world football: direct, technically brilliant, and capable of deciding matches on his own. Martin Ødegaard has developed into one of the Premier League's finest midfielders, an orchestrator whose touch and vision make Arsenal's attack flow. Gabriel Martinelli provides pace and directness on the opposite flank that defenders consistently struggle to handle.

Defensively, Arsenal are equally impressive. William Saliba — imperious, calm, almost impossible to get past — has established himself as one of the best centre-backs in Europe. David Raya in goal has added authority and ball-playing ability that the team previously lacked.

The Mental Barrier

The question that hangs over Arsenal is not one of quality — everyone in football acknowledges they are a top-four side, a Champions League side, a team capable of beating anyone. The question is whether they can sustain the belief and the form across a full 38-game season when the pressure is at its highest.

Title races are won in February and March, in the grey weeks when nothing feels exciting and the fatigue has accumulated. Arsenal have shown vulnerability in those periods. The question is whether experience — the painful education of two near-misses — has taught them how to manage those stretches better.

We are building something here. The near-misses were not failures — they were lessons. We know what it takes now. We know what we need to do. The question is whether we can execute it. — Mikel Arteta

The Competition

Manchester City, even in transition, remain formidable. Liverpool under Arne Slot have shown they can compete at the top. Chelsea's investment is beginning to produce results. The Premier League has never been harder to win — which makes Arsenal's challenge both more difficult and, in a strange way, more compelling.

The wait continues. But the belief has never been stronger.
author: SportsKeen Editorial
